posts.title: Ready before you arrive
posts.excerpt: On an event morning at Kaigi Centre the chairs are already set at 6:45, and the foyer desk opens for registration at 7:30.
posts.content:
At 6:45, Meridian Hall is still empty of delegates. Rows of chairs face the lectern. Daylight comes in from the high windows of the old warehouse. Owen Mbeki, who has the early facilities shift, walks a row and lays a notepad and a pencil at each place. There is no audience yet, and that is the point of the hour. Kaigi Centre is the conference house at 12 Quay Street, Halden Harbour. The building was a harbour customs warehouse in the 1920s. It opened as a place for association congresses and corporate offsites in 2009. Ingrid Halvorsen has been director since that first year. The work of the early shift has not become a ceremony. It is how an event day is supposed to look before anyone arrives.

The building opens at 7:00 on an event day and stays open until 23:00. Your coordinator is on site from 7:00, which means the person named on your run sheet is already in the house when the doors open. Registration is a little later. Priya Raman leads delegate services, and on a congress morning the foyer desk is ready at 7:30, with lanyards, for people walking in from the quay. The six-minute walk from Halden Central, or from the tram line 2 stop at Quay Street, fits that half hour if the trains are kind. Nothing about the morning depends on a last-minute rearrangement of the hall.

The floor they are walking into is a network of five rooms, all on one level. Meridian Hall holds 420 in theatre or 260 at banquet, and it is where plenaries and AGMs sit. The Linden Room holds 120 in classroom or 160 in theatre, for workshops, training days and parallel sessions. The Atrium holds 300 standing, for poster sessions, exhibitions and receptions. Studio Rooms 1 to 4 hold 24 to 36 people each, for breakouts and team days. The Quay Room is a boardroom for 16. A congress uses the large combination: Meridian Hall, the Atrium and the Studios are one congress floor. A smaller meeting simply does not open the hall.

The Northern Society of Hospital Pharmacists ran its annual congress this way. Four hundred and twenty delegates came for three days. Plenary sessions were in Meridian Hall, posters were in the Atrium, and breakouts used all four Studio Rooms. The Halden Teachers' Association took a different cut of the same floor: 160 people, one day, in the Linden Room, with lunch in the Atrium. Arden Logistics came for a leadership offsite, 36 people over two days, in Studio Rooms 1 and 2 with the Quay Room for the smaller table. Three gatherings, three sizes. The useful question is which rooms match the headcount, not how many events the building has ever held.

The calm at 6:45 is mostly decided weeks earlier. An enquiry gets a provisional hold for 48 hours, and the hold is free. A site visit happens on a weekday, between 9:00 and 18:00, by appointment. The contract then names the rooms, the layouts and the rate, and it takes a deposit of 30 percent. The balance is due 14 days after the event. Half a day is 60 percent of the full-day rate. Cancellation is free until 90 days before the event, 50 percent between 89 and 30 days, and 100 percent under 30 days. The run sheet that sits with the contract is what Owen's shift and Priya's desk are both following: which room, which layout, when registration opens.

Full-day rates stay in euros. Meridian Hall is €6,800, the Atrium €2,600, the Linden Room €1,900, the Quay Room €640, and each Studio Room €420. The day delegate package is €68 a person, covering a share of the room, two coffee breaks, lunch and standard AV. Lucía Romero's kitchen and Daniel Kowalski's AV team read the same headcount. Amara Nwosu's crew sets the chairs the sheet describes. Tomás Ferreira keeps the booking tied together from the first hold to the event day.

If you want to see the rooms before any of that, the open day is Saturday 14 November 2026. Hall tours run from 10:00 to 15:00, and you do not need to book. The door is 12 Quay Street. Come on a weekday, by appointment, if you already know the date and the number of people. Either way, the hall you are being shown is the same room Owen walks at 6:45, with the notepads going down before the first delegate is due.
